- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price spike is followed by model overshoot (forecast > true for 2+ consecutive days), apply downward bias of 2–5% on next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast by 3–7% to capture momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially after 10–15 days), apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, avoid large upward adjustments — forecast should lag true by 1–3 days unless strong momentum is evident.
